subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt or rebase the open fork PR, replace it with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or close that fork path before queueing another fix for this issue?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but an open conflicting fork PR still uses closing syntax and the same-repo PR was already closed as superseded, so automation should not create a competing fix branch until the branch path is chosen.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus Gateway sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt/Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, cover the missing Gateway paths, and add real behavior proof before review.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork PR even though it is conflicting, uneditable by maintainers, and has not updated since April 2026.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus Gateway sync and async displayName hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: This login merged the original session picker work and has recent adjacent Gateway session-list history, making it the strongest routing signal for the branch-path decision.
